projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: Persistent TV/media audio and dog barking reacting to outdoor sounds, combined with zero camera activity during typical daytime hours, strongly indicates either a camera system failure or an unoccupied home with background media running, warranting a system check to ensure security monitoring is active.

Continuous audio activity (speech, TV, routine sounds, and an impact) contrasts with zero camera observations, suggesting a potential camera blind spot, malfunction, or unverified occupancy. Steve should verify camera functionality or check who is home, as this gap is notable during school hours.

The highly regular, alternating barking and audio clips every minute over six minutes, paired with zero camera activity, indicates the dogs are fixated on a specific, stationary outdoor stimulus rather than random activity. This pattern suggests a recurring event like a regular delivery or neighbor, warranting a quick check to rule out any sustained outdoor disturbance.

Active multi-microphone audio (TV, speech, routine sounds) and dogs barking at outdoor stimuli, combined with zero camera activity during typical Wednesday morning hours, indicates the household is likely active in camera-blind zones while the dogs react to external events; consider verifying camera placement or status.

The recurring multi-microphone audio bursts with zero camera activity, now coinciding with dog barking and outdoor sounds, strongly indicate a system audio processing artifact or the dogs moving through non-camera blind spots rather than physical household activity. The earlier 05:47 spike to 22 connected devices alongside these bursts confirms a network wake-up event, making this a benign system artifact rather than a security concern.

The recurring pattern of simultaneous multi-microphone audio bursts with zero camera activity during early morning hours strongly indicates a localized, non-human source—likely the dogs stirring or a smart device feedback loop—rather than household movement. Monitoring this will help distinguish normal pet or system behavior from potential equipment glitches or unseen activity.

The sudden multi-microphone audio bursts at 05:47–05:50 AM, coinciding with a spike to 22 connected devices and zero camera activity, strongly indicate an automated IoT network event or synchronized smart home routine rather than household activity. This pattern suggests a scheduled system check or hub initialization that may be causing false alerts or network congestion, warranting a review of early-morning automations.

While currently benign, it warrants monitoring to rule out escalating noise or device feedback.
